history.dynasty: Vadakkumkoor kingdom (10th century, former Pandya administration); later under Travancore
history.period: 10th century (per local tradition and temple aggregators)
history.summary: The Kaduthuruthy Thaliyil Mahadeva Temple is one of the three great Shiva shrines of the Vaikom-Ettumanoor-Kaduthuruthy trio. Legend says the asura Khara (of the Ramayana's Khara-Dushana duo) performed penance to Shiva at Chidambaram and was granted three Sivalingas, which he carried southward - one in each hand and one in his mouth. When their weight forced him to rest, he set down the lingas: at Vaikom (right hand), Ettumanoor (left hand), and midway at Kaduthuruthy (the one carried in his mouth). 'Kaduthuruthy' is said to derive from 'kadichiruthy' - placed by biting. Visiting all three temples in a single day before the noon pooja is believed to fulfil one's wishes. Historically the area was under the Pandya kings in the 10th century and became the headquarters of the Vadakkumkoor dynasty; the temple is ringed by a fort (Thalikotta, 'kotta' meaning fort). About 300 years ago the temple suffered a devastating fire in which the chief priest died clutching the idol to his chest; the mandapam's wood carvings depicting the 'Karthaveerarjuneeyam' survived. Maharani Sethu Lakshmi Bai later revived the temple's 28-day festival, and after Vadakkumkoor merged into Travancore the temple passed to the Travancore Devaswom Board, under which it remains one of its major temples.

name: Kaduthuruthy Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Kaduthuruthy is a small temple town in Kottayam district, about 12 km from Vaikom on the Kottayam-Ernakulam state highway. It was the capital of the old Vadakkumkoor kingdom, is mentioned in the medieval Malayalam poem 'Unnuneeli Sandesam', and its northern and western parts are bordered by the Vembanad backwaters. It anchors the famous Vaikom-Ettumanoor-Kaduthuruthy Shiva temple trio.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 63 km; taxis available).
travel.railway: Kaduthuruthy railway station (approx. 2 km, passenger trains); Kottayam Junction (approx. 25 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: Kaduthuruthy bus stand is about 290 m from the temple. On the Kottayam-Ernakulam state highway; direct KSRTC and private buses run from Kottayam (approx. 21-25 km).

visitor_information.best_time: September to February for pleasant winter weather. The 10-day annual festival in Dhanu (December-January) is the most vibrant time to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning approx. 4:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening approx. 5:00 PM to 8:30 PM (verify - sources differ: one lists 5:00 AM-12:00 PM / 5:00-8:00 PM, another 4:00-11:00 AM / 5:00-8:00 PM). Key poojas: Nirmalyam 4:00-4:30 AM, Pantheeradi Pooja 8:00-8:30 AM, Uccha Pooja 11:00-11:30 AM, Deeparadhana 6:30-7:00 PM. Traditional Kerala dress code (dhoti/pancha without shirt for men).
